checklist.text: Open Environments in the sidebar, choose an environment, and edit a variable's key and current value.
checklist.why: the sidebar now has a full editor for the variables.

checklist.text: Open the Select environment menu, edit a current value in the quick peek, then send a request that uses it.
checklist.why: the selector now writes values straight to the saved variable.

checklist.text: Mark a variable as secret and check that its value stays masked in the quick peek and in the sidebar editor, and that the reveal toggle works.
checklist.why: secret values can now be edited in place and must stay hidden.

checklist.text: Rename a variable, then send a request that uses the old and the new name.
checklist.why: a rename is now written through the same value service.

checklist.text: Press Back in the editor and confirm the environment list returns with your edits.
Open New Collection from the sidebar and create a collection.
checklist.why: it opens from the sidebar that holds the changed tab.

checklist.text: Sign in with a team account and edit a team variable's current value.
checklist.why: team environment rows use the same editor and could not be reached signed out.

My and team environment lists: Each environment row in the sidebar lists is changed by this PR: choosing one now opens the new editor instead of only selecting it.
Secret variables when a request is sent: Secret variables are probably affected when a request is sent: their values are now also written through the secret-value service this PR extends.

Environments sidebar: The Environments sidebar is changed by this PR: choosing an environment now opens an editor with an editable key and current value for each variable. Controls involved: “Environments”.
Environment selector: The environment selector is changed by this PR: the current value of a non-secret variable can now be edited right in the quick peek. Controls involved: “Select environment”.
Variables in a GraphQL request: Variables in a GraphQL request might be affected: they are read from the same current-value service.
Secret variable values: Secret variable values will change in the new editor: they stay masked behind a reveal toggle and can now be edited in place.
“User can create a collection to organize requests.”: This requirement rests on a screen that might be affected by this PR; worth a quick look.
“User can manage environment variables used in requests.”: This requirement rests on a screen that is probably affected by this PR.
New Collection dialog: The New Collection dialog might be affected: it opens from the same sidebar as the changed Environments tab; worth a quick look.
Variables in the WebSocket address: Variables in the WebSocket address might be affected: they are read from the same current-value service; worth a quick look.
